scope: 02_rules.md:Answered question OQ-17 — Dependency vulnerability and update policy

topics.topic: Components covered by INV-050 repeated-read equality
questions: Does repeated-read equality cover the live project/project-availability component, or only the five parenthesized portal-owned components?

quotes:
2. `capability:derived_views.build_project_overview` fetches the live project
   context (`capability:registry_gateway.get_project_context`) and composes
   `capability:derived_views.build_budget_view`,
   `capability:derived_views.build_expense_view`,
   `capability:derived_views.build_progress_view` and
   `capability:derived_views.build_payment_view` with the visible photos.

- `ProjectOverview` with six availability and value pairs, deterministic for
  the same records. Produced by `module:derived_views`. No total is stored.
judgement.why: The later flow makes the project component a live Registry input and conditions equality on the same records, so a Registry change permits that component to change while the five portal-owned components remain equal.

topics.topic: Required wall-clock reading count for operations that do not use current time
questions: Must an operation that writes no timestamp and performs no current-time comparison take one wall-clock reading or none?

quotes:
- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.
judgement.why: The later module rule limits the wall reading to an operation that needs the current instant, so an operation with no timestamp or current-time comparison takes none.

topics.topic: Scope of INV-027’s prohibition on persisted derived values and the required refusal behavior
questions: Are automatically maintained, non-editable cached derived values permitted, or is any persisted derived value forbidden?
What concrete input violates INV-027 at `build_budget_view`, and what exact refusal must the Required test assert?

quotes: - INV-027: budget totals and all financial aggregates are derived at read time, never stored as editable values
- INV-027: a focused test at `build_budget_view` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.

INV-027: no table
  stores a budget total, financial aggregate or other value of a derived
  view (a content fingerprint of a received import is the identity of
  supplied content, not such a value), reading the views writes nothing,
  and after every operation that writes an owning record of a view —
  inclusion, allocations, progress, payment, plan and budget-version
  activation among them — the next read equals a recomputation from the
  stored rows.
judgement.why: The detailed check answers that every persisted derived cache is forbidden, but the texts identify no admissible violating input to `build_budget_view`, so no witness can establish two allowed refusal behaviours.

topics.topic: Whether deploy checks must account for OSV advisory changes before service startup
questions: If OSV adds, changes, or withdraws an advisory after one distribution was checked but before the service starts, must the deploy reconsider that distribution?

quotes:
3. A deploy is the start of the service from a built image. Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read in that
   same deploy; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is reused. An image in
   which a distribution has a known vulnerability is not deployed; only an
   image that passes the check is, whether the fix was a pin changed through
   the Factory route (rule 2) or a rebuild that resolved a fixed library
   under the same pins.

A distribution has a known vulnerability when an OSV entry that is not
   withdrawn lists its installed version as affected; reachability inside
   the portal is not judged case by case, so such a distribution blocks the
   deploy whatever feature the advisory concerns. A check that cannot
   complete does not pass, and the deploy waits.

- DEP-002: the deploy step judges every distribution installed in the
  built image, bound to that image's content id, against OSV data read in
  the same deploy, and starts the service only on a passing verdict about
  that same image; a listed version, unreadable or unmatchable advisory
  data, a verdict from an earlier deploy, or a verdict about another image
  does not start it
  [witness: verification:dependency_release_gate_client_portal].
judgement.divergence: One release gate treats each distribution's successful check during the deploy as final and starts the service; another rechecks or refreshes the verdict when OSV changes before startup and withholds the service, which the deployment operator observes.
judgement.why: The rules bind checks to the deploy and image but specify no common advisory snapshot or verdict instant, leaving advisory changes during the check sequence observable at startup.

witness.initial: A built image contains distributions X and Y, and OSV initially lists neither installed version as affected.
events: The deployment process checks X against OSV and receives a passing result.
OSV publishes a non-withdrawn advisory listing X's installed version as affected.
The deployment process checks Y against OSV and receives a passing result.
The deployment process reaches the service-start decision.
outcomes: The service starts because every distribution received a passing check against OSV data read during this deploy.
The service does not start because the release gate refreshes or rechecks X against the advisory state at the final deploy verdict.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and release gate

topics.topic: Whether elapsed-clock values may be retained in memory for rate limiting
questions: Does “never stored” prohibit only persistence in portal records, or also retaining the reading or a value derived from it in process memory to maintain the rate-limit window across requests?

topics.topic: Witness check covering CLK-002 clock-source, reading-count, and viewer-entry requirements
questions: Which existing witness check is bound to the CLK-002 source exclusivity, exact wall-reading count, and viewer-entry elapsed-reading requirements?
